bullets.title: Tech sector on pace for back-to-back 10%+ monthly gains — last seen in 2009
bullets.body: The S&P 500 Technology sector is tracking consecutive 10%+ monthly gains, a streak only matched three other times historically: post-GFC recovery (Mar-Apr 2009), the dot-com bubble (Nov-Dec 1998, Nov-Dec 1999), and the dot-com crash bounces (Oct-Nov 2001, Oct-Nov 2002). The S&P 500 also hit a new all-time high on the session.

bullets.title: 7Y Treasury auction draws 3rd-highest foreign demand on record; yield rises 11.5bps
bullets.body: The 7-year note auction cleared at 4.290% (WI 4.291%, 0.1bps stop-through), with indirect bidders surging to 78.4% from 58.4% prior — the 3rd highest foreign demand on record. Direct bidder participation collapsed to 11.2% from 30.0%, and the bid-to-cover held at 2.52x.

bullets.title: April PCE cooler than expected at core; YoY inflation remains elevated
bullets.body: April core PCE rose 0.2% m/m (vs. 0.3% est.), the mildest gain in five months, though the 3-month annualized rate sits at 3.8% and the 12-month at 3.3%. Headline PCE rose 0.4% m/m (vs. 0.5% est.) and 3.8% YoY. Personal income printed flat (0.0% vs. 0.4% est.) as spending held at +0.5%.

bullets.title: Q1 GDP revised down to 1.6%; macro data broadly soft outside durable goods
bullets.body: The second estimate for Q1 2026 GDP came in at +1.6% q/q annualized, below the +2.0% consensus and prior reading. Mixed macro day: durable goods orders beat at +7.9% (est. 4.0%), but core capital goods orders missed at -1.1% (est. +0.4%), new home sales missed at 622K (est. 660K), and jobless claims edged above forecast at 215K.

bullets.title: Fed's Musalem signals easing bias no longer appropriate; neutral rate higher
bullets.body: Fed's Musalem stated the prior easing bias is 'no longer consistent with risks,' flagging risks that inflation may not converge to target and that rates may need to rise in some scenarios. He noted rising Treasury yields mostly reflect a higher expected neutral rate, not recession fears. Williams separately projected near-term headline inflation at 4%, core at 3%, with tariff effects peaking in coming months.

bullets.title: Snowflake surges on $6B AWS Graviton deal; Dan Ives calls it AI monetization positive
bullets.body: Snowflake committed $6 billion over five years to AWS Graviton CPUs, driving SNOW to an all-time high (+9% on the day). Wedbush's Dan Ives calls it 'a major positive for software sector and AI monetization narrative,' citing Snowflake's infrastructure as a competitive moat. CRPO and product revenue growth are tracking to mid-30s.

bullets.title: NVDA forward P/E at 17x vs. Costco 45x; Jensen Huang teases 'surprising new product'
bullets.body: NVDA trades at just 17x forward P/E versus Costco at 45x and Walmart at 36x, drawing attention to relative valuation. Separately, Jensen Huang at a dinner signaled NVIDIA has 'a surprising new product' not yet disclosed publicly. GTC Taipei keynote is June 1 focusing on physical AI and infrastructure scaling.

bullets.title: NVIDIA and Lilly announce $1B joint AI drug discovery lab; NVDA driving InP laser 20x scale demand
bullets.body: NVIDIA and Eli Lilly are jointly investing up to $1 billion over five years in a co-innovation AI lab for drug discovery. Separately, Rosenblatt checks confirm NVIDIA is pushing for 20x InP laser capacity scaling from 2025-2030, with supply chain vendors agreeing to 12x — creating a significant optical supply bottleneck.

bullets.title: Marvell: FY28 DC guidance seen as conservative; upgraded to #1 long by Hedgeye
bullets.body: Marvell raised FY27/FY28 outlooks on AI interconnect strength. Hedgeye upgraded MRVL to its #1 long position, while one analyst noted guidance may be conservative and their growth assumptions remain ahead of the company. Stock has roughly doubled since the last print.

bullets.title: Micron EVP: Meaningful memory supply won't arrive until late 2027, pricing power through 2028
bullets.body: Micron's EVP and Chief Business Officer Sumit Sadana stated that 'even with all the new investments,' meaningful new memory chip supply will only start coming online in late 2027, with the real ramp in 2028 — supporting multi-year pricing power for DRAM and HBM.

bullets.title: SNDK hits all-time high (+6%); HBF commercialization as DRAM alternative cited as long-term thesis
bullets.body: SNDK reached a new all-time high, up ~6% on the session. The bull thesis centers on HBF (High Bandwidth Flash) commercializing into a viable DRAM substitute for KV cache, which could drive years of upside — especially as HBM4 thermal challenges create constraints for existing suppliers.

bullets.title: SMCI +14% on Taiwan authority collaboration; DELL cited as catch-up trade
bullets.body: Super Micro surged ~14% intraday after announcing collaboration with Taiwanese authorities on server technology diversion prevention, resulting in 3 arrests. One trader calls DELL a catch-up trade in response to SMCI's move.

bullets.title: ARM, NVDA, SNOW at all-time highs on CPU adoption momentum
bullets.body: ARM reached an all-time high as NVDA and AMZN are both expected to significantly increase orders of ARM CPUs. The Snowflake $6B AWS Graviton commitment further reinforces ARM's secular demand story. Multiple names in the ecosystem hitting simultaneous ATHs.

bullets.title: Meta CEO hints at cloud computing entry if datacenter capacity exceeds internal needs
bullets.body: Mark Zuckerberg signaled Meta could enter the cloud computing market if it builds excess datacenter capacity — a meaningful strategic pivot that would pit Meta against AMZN AWS, GOOGL, and MSFT Azure in enterprise AI infrastructure.

bullets.title: Trade Desk flagged as biggest loser in Publicis/LiveRamp deal; Walmart diversifying to Yahoo DSP
bullets.body: LightShed Partners characterizes TTD as the 'biggest loser' in Publicis's LiveRamp deal. Separately, Walmart is actively diversifying programmatic ad spend away from The Trade Desk toward Yahoo's DSP, which leverages first-party data from email, fantasy sports, and finance properties.

bullets.title: Microsoft to debut task-specialized AI models and new coding model next week
bullets.body: Microsoft is set to release specialized task-focused AI models and a new coding model as early as next week per The Information. Microsoft's AI chief separately claimed an 18-month timeline to automate all white-collar work.

bullets.title: Okta and enterprise agent authentication emerging as AI infrastructure play
bullets.body: One trader initiated 'teaser positions' in identity names OKTA (down 60% from ATH) and SAIL on the thesis that enterprise AI agents will require identification, tracking, and authorization — framing identity as core AI infrastructure as agentic deployments scale.

bullets.title: AWS achieves 33% throughput gain, 40% power reduction with Resilient Network Graphs at hyperscale
bullets.body: Amazon achieved a significant data center networking breakthrough by deploying flat 'Resilient Network Graphs' architecture at hyperscale, delivering 33% better throughput and 40% less network power consumption — potentially a meaningful capex efficiency differentiator.

bullets.title: Gamma squeeze driving S&P to new highs; SMH dealers in negative gamma with violent downside risk
bullets.body: Analysts note a gamma squeeze mechanism pushing stocks to new all-time highs. Simultaneously, $SMH dealers are holding negative gamma with a surging put/call ratio, suggesting downside moves could be violent — with June OPEX expected to relieve the pressure.

bullets.title: US personal savings rate collapses to 2.6%; credit card delinquencies at 13-year high
bullets.body: The US personal savings rate dropped to 2.6%, the lowest since April 2008 (30-year average: 5.7%), while 13.1% of credit card balances are now 90+ days delinquent — the highest since 2011. Real wage growth has turned negative and disposable income fell for three consecutive months.
